standard_prerequisites.name: An associated prime of a module over a ring is the annihilator of some element, and localization is exact
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element whose annihilator is the prime in the first direction, and the element of the localization whose annihilator is the localized prime in the second.

standard_prerequisites.name: The stalk of a quasi-coherent module on an affine open at a prime is the localization of the module of sections at that prime, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the localized module with the stalk so that association at the point follows from association at the prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a finitely generated prime ideal contained in the annihilator up to localization there is an element outside the prime killing the quotient
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades association of the localized element to association of an honest element of the module of sections.

standard_prerequisites.name: In a locally Noetherian scheme the coordinate rings of affine opens are Noetherian, cited from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes every prime finitely generated, which is the hypothesis of the converse direction.

core_obligations: First direction: if the prime p is associated to M, take an element m of M annihilated exactly by p; exactness of localization makes the localized prime the annihilator of m/1 in the localization, which is the stalk of F at x, so x is associated to F (proof lines 86-95).

Second direction: if x is associated to F and p is finitely generated, take an element of the localization whose annihilator is the localized prime and write it as m/f with f outside p; the annihilator I of m satisfies the same localization, whence I is contained in p and the localization of p modulo I vanishes (proof lines 97-104).

Use finite generation of p to find an element g outside p annihilating p modulo I, so that the annihilator of the product gm is exactly p, which makes p associated to M and proves the converse (proof lines 104-108).

Locally Noetherian case: the coordinate ring of an affine open is then Noetherian, so every prime is finitely generated and the two directions combine into the stated equivalence (proof lines 110-116).
proof_roadmap: Compare association at a prime with association at the corresponding point by localizing an element with the given annihilator (proof lines 86-95).

For the converse, lift an element of the localization to an element of the module, control the annihilator modulo the prime, and use finite generation to adjust the element so that its annihilator is exactly the prime (proof lines 97-116).
difficulty_reason: The lemma relates the associated primes of the module of sections over an affine open to the associated points of the sheaf, with the converse needing the prime to be finitely generated and the locally Noetherian case following (statement lines 67-84). The counted proof gives both directions explicitly: the forward direction localizes an element with the prescribed annihilator and identifies the localization of the module of sections with the stalk, while the converse lifts an element of the localization, studies the annihilator modulo the prime, and uses finite generation of the prime to adjust the element so that its annihilator is exactly the prime (proof lines 86-116). It is H2: the argument is a complete and self-contained piece of local algebra, with no independent research-level content.
